issues.display_title: Issue #41: Add panorama loading spinner & dark mode background
issues.main_description_html:
Improve the Preview experience for panorama images.

Add a loading animation (spinner) so users get clear feedback while a large panorama is opening, instead of a blank or frozen-looking screen. Also add a proper dark background when dark mode is on, so the view is comfortable and consistent with the rest of the app.

Impact: clearer feedback during loading and a more polished look in dark mode.

DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-07-01.at.15.02.07.mov

Verdict: Passed. The installed Windows application (GoThru Photo Studio 1.1.10) shows a loading spinner during panorama replacement and uses a dark viewer/loading background in dark mode.

Test data Existing tester panorama data in the Preview grid
Account Tester GoThru account; credentials were not displayed in evidence

TC-41-03 Gray-box Trace real UI state to implementation behavior The overlay clears after the media is ready New panorama rendered normally after the loading state Passed
TC-41-04 White-box Review Preview loading and theme wiring Spinner is tied to media readiness and dark styles are applied Main.tsx and PanoramaViewer.tsx render the spinner/overlay; dark:bg-black is used; global dark backgrounds are defined in index.css Passed

issues.display_title: Issue #29: Handle Issue Main Viewer Flashes White Screen During Loading/Transitions
issues.main_description_html:
A jarring UX issue has been reported in the GoThru Photo Studio desktop application (v1.1.2). The user experiences a "strange flash to a white screen" within the main viewing area.

Because the application utilizes a dark theme, this sudden bright white flash is highly disruptive to the user's eyes. This typically happens when the viewer component is unmounting/remounting, transitioning between images, or during the brief loading period before the canvas/WebGL context fully initializes and renders the panorama.

Screenshot / User Report

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Navigating between images or opening the main viewer no longer produces a white flash.
  2. The background of the viewer remains consistent with the application's overall dark theme during any loading or transition states.

DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-07-01.at.15.02.07.mov

QA Summary - Bug (2026-08-27)

Verdict

Bug reproduced from real-device tester report. Rapidly alternating panorama navigation forward/backward and then closing Preview force-closes the desktop application. This supersedes the earlier Passed verdict, which covered only an abrupt force-close black-frame observation and did not exercise rapid navigation followed by Preview close.

Reproduction

Step Action Expected Actual Result
1 Open Preview with a folder containing panorama images Viewer remains stable Viewer opens Pass
2 Navigate forward and backward rapidly between panoramas In-flight media transitions remain safe Multiple texture loads/prefetches overlap Risk observed
3 Close/switch away from Preview while transitions are in flight Preview closes without terminating the application Application force-closes Fail

QA Test Summary

Area Method Finding Result
Crash reproduction Black-box real-device validation by tester Rapid back/forward panorama navigation then Preview close terminates the app Fail
Async texture lifecycle Gray-box source-flow review ImageSphere starts visible and neighbor texture loads; cleanup only marks the React effect cancelled Fail candidate aligned with repro
Resource handling White-box source review textureCache may dispose entries after its bounded cache evicts them while asynchronous texture loading is still unresolved; there is no cancellation/disposal coordination for the loader on Preview unmount Fail candidate aligned with repro
Existing unit coverage Unit-test review Cache tests cover LRU, protection of a specified current URL, and failed-load retry; they do not cover rapid navigation plus unmount/Preview close with pending texture loads Gap

Code Review Evidence

File Relevant behavior
src/renderer/features/preview/ImageSphere.tsx Loads active texture and prefetches neighbours asynchronously. Effect cleanup sets cancelled, but does not abort an existing THREE.TextureLoader request or coordinate pending decode with Canvas disposal.
src/renderer/features/preview/textureCache.ts Bounded LRU eviction schedules texture.dispose() from stored promises; it has no owner/reference tracking for pending or actively transitioning textures.
src/renderer/features/preview/PanoramaViewer.tsx React Three Fiber Canvas unmounts when Preview is closed, intersecting with in-flight texture work.
src/renderer/features/preview/Preview.tsx Keyboard navigation applies each Arrow/A/D action immediately; no transition guard or cancellation is present before closing/switching the viewer.

Test Methods and Confusion Matrix

Method Coverage Result
Black box Real-device sequence: rapid panorama back/forward navigation then close Preview Fail - force-close reported
Gray box Renderer state, navigation, cache, and unmount flow tracing Fail candidate supported
White box Async texture loader, cache eviction, cleanup, and unit-test coverage inspection Lifecycle protection gap found
Confusion matrix TP: rapid navigation plus close causes app termination; TN: normal/isolated close not assessed in this report; FP: not applicable; FN: earlier force-close-only test missed this sequence Repro scenario confirmed

Developer Handoff

Investigate the Panorama ImageSphere lifecycle under rapid source changes and Canvas unmount. Prioritize cancellation or ownership/ref-count handling for pending loads, prevent disposal of textures still usable by the transitioning renderer, and add a deterministic test for rapid navigation followed by Preview unmount/close.

Evidence and Scope

The real-device failure was supplied by the tester. The supplied attachment could not be independently downloaded from this QA environment at the time of review (GitHub attachment endpoint returned HTTP 404), so this report does not claim byte-verified video evidence. No account, file, or other persistent test data was modified.

QA Decision

2026-08-27.14-10-47.mp4

Result: Bug. The prior QA Passed conclusion is invalid for the newly exercised rapid-navigation-and-close scenario.

issues.display_title: Issue #48: Pin framer-motion to v11 (fix Select warning)
issues.main_description_html:

A newer version of the library introduced a compatibility warning. Pinning to the stable version keeps dropdowns clean and predictable.

issues.display_title: Issue #77: Modernize the app's internal data-handling layer for reliability
issues.main_description_html:
Second step in the ongoing front-end cleanup effort (builds on the code quality setup from the previous step).

The app keeps track of things like which files are loaded, what's currently being edited, and user settings using a central internal data store. This step upgrades how that store is accessed throughout the app, adding safety checks that catch a whole class of bugs automatically before they ever reach users.

What changed for users: Nothing — this is entirely behind-the-scenes work. No visual or functional changes.

Why it matters: Reduces the risk of subtle bugs in file handling, editing tools, and settings, and makes the codebase easier and safer to build new features on top of.

Part of the larger front-end refactor initiative. Builds on the code quality setup (previous issue). See PR #75.

Bug confirmed: the current source branch is not buildable.

issues.display_title: Issue #30: Implement Persist Login State and API Keys Across App Updates
issues.main_description_html:
A user reported a frustrating experience during the app update process. Because they had to uninstall the application to update it, their local data was wiped. As a result, they lost their active login session and their saved Nano Banana API key, forcing them to re-authenticate and reconfigure their settings from scratch.

We need to ensure that user credentials and critical configurations are preserved between updates and uninstalls, providing a seamless transition to newer versions.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. When a user updates the application (even if it involves a manual uninstall and reinstall), their login session is preserved, and they remain logged in.
  2. The Nano Banana API key is successfully retained and automatically loaded into the new version's configuration.
  3. User credentials and API keys are stored securely in an OS-appropriate persistent directory.

Result by developer: Data preserved from old (Electron) project → new (Tauri) project

Old Electron app stored NeDB files at os.tmpdir()/gothru-photo-studio/[version]/*.db — a temp dir, which is why data got wiped on uninstall/reinstall. Tauri build already has a one-time importer (src-tauri/src/migration.rs) that reads those legacy files on first launch and moves them into the new persistent store (SQLite DB + tauri-plugin-store under the OS app-data dir). Data carried over:

  • Accounts / login session (accounts.db → accounts table): email, token, type (panorra | gothru | streetview), isDefault, refeshToken, username.
  • Settings (settings.db → settings.json store): all fields except NeDB meta (_id, id, createdAt, updatedAt), including:
    • apiKeys — array of { id, keyName, apiKey, model, valid }, this is where the Nano Banana API key lives.
    • hotkeys, theme, language, mapMode, mapServer, viewMode, gridSize, positionFolderPanel, showMap, setLastOpenedLocation, defaultLocation, rotationDegree, rotationDuration, rotationDirection, autoClearCache, autoClearCacheDays, cache, currentVersionBinaries.
  • Bookmarks (bookmarks.db → bookmarks table): name, path, color.
  • Favorites (favorites.db → favorites table): filePath, createdAt, updatedAt.

Migration runs once per install (guarded by a .migrated sentinel file in the app-data dir) and only triggers if the legacy temp folder is still present at first launch — so it does not help if Windows/the OS has already cleared the temp dir before the Tauri build ever runs. That gap is what this issue needs to close: the underlying storage location itself (not just a one-time import) must live in an OS-appropriate persistent directory from the start, so subsequent Tauri-to-Tauri updates never depend on a temp-dir import again.

QA Tester Summary - 2026-08-26

Verdict: Bug confirmed - Acceptance Criterion 3 not met.

Scope and evidence

Area Result Evidence
Persistent location Pass Production Tauri storage is under the Windows per-user app-data location: AppData\\Roaming\\com.gothru.photostudio.
Login-session persistence Partial Account/session records are migrated into gothru.db (accounts table). No uninstall/reinstall was run because it would delete shared local application data.
Nano Banana API-key persistence Partial apiKeys are migrated and retained in settings.json. No real API key value was read or exposed.
Secure credential storage Fail Source review found gothru.db (SQLite) for account tokens and settings.json through tauri-plugin-store for apiKeys; no OS credential vault, Stronghold, or encryption layer was found.

Reproduction / verification

Step Expected Actual Status
1. Inspect the configured Tauri app-data storage path Data resides in an OS-appropriate persistent directory gothru.db and settings.json exist under the per-user Windows app-data directory Pass
2. Trace account migration and storage Login credentials use secure OS-backed storage migration.rs imports account token and refeshToken into the SQLite accounts table Fail
3. Trace API-key migration and storage Nano Banana API key uses secure OS-backed storage migration.rs copies apiKeys; settings.rs persists them in settings.json through tauri-plugin-store Fail
4. Search the storage implementation for a protection layer Encryption / OS credential vault is used for secrets No implementation of Windows Credential Manager, OS keychain, Stronghold, or equivalent encryption was found Fail

Test methods and coverage

Method Coverage Result
Black-box / real installed-app inspection Verified the actual persistent data location without exposing tester credentials or API-key values Pass for persistence location
Gray-box Correlated installed data artifacts with Tauri app-data configuration and migration behavior Fail for secure-at-rest handling
White-box code review Reviewed src-tauri/src/migration.rs, src-tauri/src/commands/settings.rs, and account SQLite repository wiring Bug confirmed
Confusion matrix Positive: persistent app-data exists. Negative: no secure credential store/encryption. Expected secure storage was absent, so this is a true positive defect. Bug confirmed

Developer action requested

Store access tokens, refresh tokens, and Nano Banana API keys in an OS-backed secure credential mechanism (for Windows, Credential Manager/DPAPI; platform equivalents on macOS/Linux) or an encrypted secret store with protected key handling. Keep non-secret preferences in normal app-data storage.

Test limitations

Item Limitation
Manual uninstall/reinstall Not executed because it is destructive to existing local application data and requires explicit approval plus a cleanup/restore plan.
Runtime test commands Frontend test runner currently fails loading TypeScript modules; typecheck lacks react-image-crop; Rust cargo is unavailable on PATH. These environment/baseline blockers are separate from the confirmed storage defect.
